type assertion (as).description:
TS 1.0 (`as` syntax: TS 1.6)
value as Type
Tells the compiler to treat `value` as `Type` without a runtime check — use only when you know more than the type checker does; `<Type>value` is the older, JSX-incompatible syntax this replaced.

satisfies operator.description:
TS 4.9
value satisfies Type
Validates that `value` is assignable to `Type` *without* widening its inferred type to `Type` — keeps literal/narrow inference (unlike `: Type` or `as Type`) while still catching typos/excess-property errors.

non-null assertion.description:
TS 2.0
value!
Asserts to the compiler that `value` is not `null`/`undefined` at this point, without a runtime check — use sparingly, prefer real narrowing where possible.

type-only import.description:
TS 3.8 (export type: TS 3.8)
import type { X } from 'module'
Imports guaranteed to be erased at compile time — makes the type-only intent explicit and plays well with `isolatedModules`/bundler transpilation.
